claims.why_uncovered: The status item takes the federal filing status unchanged and cites only the general rule ("In most cases, you must use the same filing status you used on your federal return"). Nothing in the encoding covers the exception for a joint federal filer whose spouse is a nonresident or part-year resident of New York. No question asks about the spouses' residency, and no refusal covers the case. The HANDLED ELSEWHERE refusals are about federal filing-status tests and nonresident aliens for the EIC, so they do not cover it either. In this case New York requires married filing separately, or a joint return as if both spouses were residents, so the federal status cannot simply be carried over.

claims.quote: If you received foreign income but did not receive a federal Form W-2, you must complete Form IT-2.
claims.why_uncovered: The encoding builds one IT-2 record per Form W-2. Every question asks for amounts from a W-2 or W-2c. Nothing asks whether the filer had foreign income without a W-2, and nothing builds an IT-2 record for that income. No refusal covers that case either. The HANDLED ELSEWHERE list covers only withholding reported on Forms 1099-R, 1099-G and W-2G, not foreign income with no W-2.

claims.why_uncovered: The only Item A exception the encoding handles is the resident/nonresident spouse case (ny_it201.gate.spouse_nonresident). Two other exceptions let a couple who filed a joint federal return file married filing separately in New York: a spouse whose whereabouts are unknown, and a spouse who refuses to sign. No question asks about either situation and no refusal covers it. The filing status therefore always follows the federal one, which drives the standard deduction, the tax computation, and the household and school tax credit tables.

claims.quote: However, if your 2024 New York adjusted gross income was more than $150,000 (or $75,000 if you are married filing separately for 2025) and you are not a farmer or a fisherman, your 2025 prepayments must equal at least 110% of your 2024 New York income tax based on a 12-month return.
claims.why_uncovered: ny_it201.ask.prior_agi_high asks only about the 2024 New York AGI threshold. Nothing asks whether the filer is a farmer or fisherman, so the 110% requirement is applied to farmers and fishermen too. Their 100% safe harbor is not recognized, and the estimated-penalty determination can come out wrong (or be refused) for them.

claims.why_uncovered: The status item is bound directly to the federal filing status. It cites only the general rule ("In most cases, you must use the same filing status you used on your federal return"). Nothing asks whether one spouse on a joint federal return was a New York resident and the other a nonresident or part-year resident. Nothing refuses that case either. In that case New York requires either married filing separately (status ③, the single schedule) or a joint return as if both were residents (status ②). The encoding would just carry the federal joint status through to the married filing jointly schedule. No refusal on the HANDLED ELSEWHERE list covers this New York mixed-residency exception. The f1040 filing-status refusals only test federal marriage facts.
